decision_maker: Executive Member for Highways and Environmental Services
purpose:
The scheme proposes a package
of highway improvements to make travel in Partington safer, easier
and more accessible. The aim is to give residents better choices
for short local journeys, reduce reliance on the car where
possible, improve local connections and create a safer and
healthier environment.
content:
The scheme proposes a package
of highway improvements to make travel in Partington safer, easier
and more accessible. The aim is to give residents better choices
for short local journeys, reduce reliance on the car where
possible, improve local connections and create a safer and
healthier environment.

1)   
That the results of the consultation and the
objections received be noted.
 
2)   
That, following careful consideration, the
objections are not upheld except where they are addressed through
the targeted amendments set out in the report.
 
3)   
That authorisation be given to remove Schedule 7
– No Right Turn Order from the Traffic Regulation Order, as
advertised.
 
4)   
That authorisation be given to make and implement
Schedules 1 to 6 of the Traffic Regulation Order, as advertised and
as shown on the drawings attached at Appendix 1, subject to final
drawing reference check.
 
5)   
That the detailed design stage considers alternative
opportunities, such as echelon-style parking or alternative parking
layouts, to optimise parking provision on Broadway where any such
arrangement would need to satisfy technical requirements relating
to visibility, available carriageway width, vehicle swept paths,
drainage, footway protection, refuse collection, emergency access
and safe entry and exit movements.
 
6)   
That localised “keep clear” markings are
introduced where required to maintain safe access and visibility,
including at Wood Lane / A6144 Warburton Lane, if confirmed through
detailed design.
 
7)   
That all objectors be informed of the
decision.

The recommendations are based
on the conclusion that the scheme will deliver significant road
safety, accessibility and sustainable travel benefits, particularly
for vulnerable road users such as pedestrians, wheelchair users,
people with pushchairs, children, older residents and cyclists. The
proposals are supported by consultation feedback, active travel
survey evidence, collision and speed data, and are considered a
necessary and proportionate package of measures to address
severance, improve crossing opportunities and encourage safer local
journeys.
 
All objections have been
carefully considered and, where appropriate, amendments have been
made, including removing the proposed right-turn ban from Bailey
Lane in response to local access concerns. However, the remaining
measures are considered integral to achieving the scheme's
objectives and are therefore recommended to proceed substantially
as advertised.

Throughout the development of
the scheme, a range of options were considered in response to
issues raised through consultation and design review. On Broadway,
opportunities to retain or increase parking provision through
echelon-style parking arrangements were explored. However, this
option was discounted at the current stage due to highway safety
concerns associated with vehicles reversing into and out of parking
spaces on a route that is anticipated to experience increased
traffic flows as a result of the
approved strategic development at the western end of Broadway. Such
manoeuvres could increase conflict between vehicles, pedestrians
and cyclists and would not support the scheme's safety
objectives.
 
Similarly, the original
proposal to prohibit right-turn movements from Bailey Lane onto
A6144 Warburton Lane was intended to support the operation of the
new crossing and cycle infrastructure. However, following careful
consideration of objections relating to local access, journey
lengths and potential traffic displacement onto surrounding
residential streets, the Council has adopted a balanced approach by
removing the proposed right-turn ban whilst retaining the one-way
arrangement and associated active travel improvements.
 
Aside from these targeted
amendments, the remaining measures are considered integral to the
delivery of the scheme's objectives. The package of crossings,
traffic calming, speed management, junction improvements, footway
upgrades and cycle infrastructure has been developed as a coherent
set of interventions designed to improve safety, accessibility and
connectivity. These measures are particularly important for
vulnerable road users, including pedestrians, wheelchair users,
people with pushchairs or mobility aids, children travelling to
school, older residents and cyclists, and are therefore recommended
to proceed as proposed.

None.

purpose:
The
Talbot Road, Warwick Road and Brian Statham Way Junction is a
Trafford Council (TC) promoted scheme, to be funded through tranche
1 of the City Region Sustainable Transport Settlement (CRSTS),
Government funding provided to Greater Manchester for transport
improvements.
 
This
junction is along a key route for people walking, wheeling and
cycling between Stretford, Old Trafford and the city centre. It is
also a busy area for people travelling to and from Old Trafford
football and cricket grounds, nearby tram stops, education
facilities and new developments. The scheme has also been
prioritised because it is the only remaining major signal controlled junction on the Stretford Cycleway
that has not yet been upgraded.
 
The
report summarises the outcomes of the consultation of the proposed
Talbot Road, Warwick Road and Brian Statham Way Junction and to
recommend that the proposed scheme and progress to detailed design
stage and, subject to all necessary CRSTS business case approvals,
proceed to delivery as per programme of works.
content:
The
Talbot Road, Warwick Road and Brian Statham Way Junction is a
Trafford Council (TC) promoted scheme, to be funded through tranche
1 of the City Region Sustainable Transport Settlement (CRSTS),
Government funding provided to Greater Manchester for transport
improvements.
 
This
junction is along a key route for people walking, wheeling and
cycling between Stretford, Old Trafford and the city centre. It is
also a busy area for people travelling to and from Old Trafford
football and cricket grounds, nearby tram stops, education
facilities and new developments. The scheme has also been
prioritised because it is the only remaining major signal controlled junction on the Stretford Cycleway
that has not yet been upgraded.
 
The
report summarises the outcomes of the consultation of the proposed
Talbot Road, Warwick Road and Brian Statham Way Junction and to
recommend that the proposed scheme and progress to detailed design
stage and, subject to all necessary CRSTS business case approvals,
proceed to delivery as per programme of works.

1.   
That the content and findings of the consultation
report, be noted.

 
2.   
That it be noted that the scheme, factoring in input
from the consultation, approve progression to detailed design and,
subject to the required CRSTS business case approvals,
delivery.

 
3.   
That the programme as set out in Section 5 of the
report, be noted.

 
4.   
That the Corporate Director of Place, in
consultation with the Director of Finance and Systems, be delegated
authority to negotiate and finalise the grant funding arrangements,
construction contracts and any other contracts or documents
required to implement the decision.

 
5.   
That the Director of Legal and Governance, be
delegated authority to enter any contracts or other documents
required to implement the decision.  

The
Talbot Road, Warwick Road and Brian Statham Way Junction scheme
will support and encourage sustainable modes of transport for the
surrounding communities, help to deliver Trafford’s vision
for inclusive and accessible neighbourhoods and provide both the
local and wider connections to other high quality strategic walking
and cycling infrastructure along GM’s Bee Active
Network.
 
This
report forms part of an approval process of securing CRSTS funding
for the delivery of the scheme.
 
It
is recommended that the Talbot Road, Warwick Road and Brian Statham
Way Junction scheme progress to detailed design stage and, subject
to all necessary CRSTS business case approvals, proceed to delivery
as it supports Trafford’s objectives of providing alternative
sustainable active travel modes of transport being used across the
Borough that will benefit health and wellbeing and air
quality.

The
alternative options would include retaining the existing
arrangements. This would leave a significant gap in the active
travel network; it would not address current safety and operational
challenges and miss the opportunity to accommodate future growth
and increasing pedestrian demand associated with ongoing
regeneration and major events in the area.
 
A
second alternative would involve reducing the scope of the scheme
altogether; this would risk the scheme, not achieving its desired
objectives, limiting opportunities to improve safety, accessibility
and connectivity for people walking, wheeling and cycling, while
failing to address existing pressures associated with high
pedestrian demand during matchdays and major events. This also
risks not demonstrating sufficient economic benefits to secure the
funding criteria and well as potentially not future proofing this
area as development occurs around it as forecast.
 
Both
alternatives are missed opportunities to achieve the stated
outcomes as in the councils Walking, Wheeling, and Cycling strategy
of improving infrastructure and support towards reducing carbon
emissions. They would also impact on Trafford’s reputation
for securing future funding bids for other sustainable grant Active
Travel opportunities that aim to encourage residents to be more
active and supporting people out of poverty by enabling affordable
transport.
topline: The Executive Member for Climate Change has decided to approve the Talbot Road, Warwick Road and Brian Statham Way Junction scheme to progress towards improving sustainable transport in Trafford.

purpose:
The
Council has been contacted by the Police and Ward Members who have
requested that consideration be given to the introduction of
parking restrictions to address the access and road safety issues
on John Gilbert Way, Europa Gate/Access to World Freight Centre,
Pomona Strand, Cornbrook Road,
Westinghouse Road, Fraser Place, Europa Circle & Europa
Way.
These
locations experience high levels of parking demand associated with
commuter activity and, significantly, during event periods at the
nearby stadium. On match and event days, the surrounding highway
network experiences substantial congestion and increased parking
demand, with vehicles frequently parking in an obstructive manner
on carriageways and footways. This results in obstruction, reduced
visibility, and restricted access for all road users, including
service and emergency vehicles. Even vehicles waiting for a limited
duration, for instance for loading/unloading, can result in
prolonged occupation of the highway, contributing to congestion,
obstruction, and reduced network efficiency.
The
proposals seek to introduce ‘No Waiting at Any Time’,
‘No Waiting & No Loading at Any Time’ and ‘No
Stopping at Any Time’ restrictions to deter inconsiderate and
obstructive parking, to improve access, visibility, and the safe
operation of the highway network for all road users. The inclusion
of loading restrictions is necessary to prevent obstruction on
these key routes.
In
addition, the ongoing development on Cornbrook Road will require a further review of the
Traffic Regulation Order on completion of construction, to enable
suitable arrangements for drop-off and lay-by servicing. No
completion dates for these works have yet been
confirmed.
The
proposals are shown on drawings numbered E9405-01 - E9405-08 and
detailed in the schedules within this report.

1.   
That authorisation be given to advertise the
intention to introduce the Traffic Regulation Orders as detailed in

as soon as practicable.

 
2.   
That any objections maintained be reported back to
Members for consideration.

As
part of Trafford Council’s target to meet demand for new
dwellings the former Magistrate’s Court site in Sale has been
identified for redevelopment. The development site is extensive,
encompassing the whole of the former Magistrates Court and car
parking area together with the adjacent Ashton Lane & York Road
gyratory which is now considered unnecessary from a highway network
perspective.
 
The
development will include the construction of
46-three-and-four-bedroom houses and 38-one-and-two-bedroom
apartments in two apartment blocks. These modern dwellings will
provide a sought-after addition to the existing housing stock
within this popular part of Trafford and will also aesthetically
compliment homes and business premises within the immediate
locality.
 
The
intention of these traffic management proposals is to ensure
suitable and safe access to the development and to ensure that the
development is accommodated safely and successfully within the
highway network.
 

To
do nothing would not target the safety and accessibility concerns
for highway users, that the new development has the potential to create.

content:
To
provide an update on changes to the council’s highway weed
control programme and explain the move from one annual herbicide
application to two targeted applications, while maintaining the
commitment to minimising chemical use and protecting the
environment.

1)   
That a trial of the proposed changes to the annual
weed control programme for 2026, be agreed.

 
2)   
That a report on the outcomes of the trial and
recommended next steps be presented to the Executive Member for
Highways, Environmental and Traded Services, in Autumn / Winter
2026.

It
is recommended that it is agreed to trial two sprays of herbicide
on hard surfaces across Trafford in 2026. This will allow the
service to review if this improves the effectiveness of the
treatment and reduce the visibility of weeds across
Trafford.
 
The
service will monitor the effectiveness of the trial using a
combination of monitoring data provided by the contractor, on-site
monitoring of the effectiveness of the two treatments, supported by
photographic evidence and analysis of customer data including
service requests and complaints.
 
During this trial the service will continue to monitor the
market for new technologies.

The
Council could continue to treat weeds with one annual spray of
herbicide. However, this is not recommended due to the poor
performance of one spray over the recent years and the increasing
visibility of weeds on the highway.
topline: The Executive Member for Highways, Environmental, and Traded Services has decided to trial two targeted herbicide applications for the council's highway weed control programme.

content:
This report seeks approval to
continue to fund two posts, whose contracts end on 31 March 2026,
from Trafford’s EDRG allocation 2026/2027. Being as EDRG
allocations for each local authority are yet to be formally
approved by the GMCA, and overall proposals to utilise EDRG will be
subject to Executive approval in June 2026,  delegated
authority is sought to extend these posts to the end of March 2027
in advance to provide security for the two staff members and ensure
continuity of delivery.

(1)              
That the continued funding of the Project Officer
and Social Value Co Ordinator posts from the anticipated EDRG
allocation 2026/2027 for the period 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027,
be approved, subject to receipt of the EDRG grant from Greater
Manchester Combined Authority.

 
(2)              
That it be noted that the decision to make the posts
permanent will be taken by the Corporate Director of Place under
the Scheme of Delegation to Officers (Part 3, Section 4) in
accordance with the Council's HR policies.
 
(3)              
That the Corporate Director of Place, in
consultation with the Director of Finance and Systems, be
authorised to take such steps as are necessary to give effect to
this decision.
 
(4)              
That the decision be deemed as urgent and not
subject to call-in, for the following reason:
 

The contracts of the two officer posts expire on 31
March 2026. Any delay caused by the call-in process would seriously
prejudice the Council's interests by creating a gap in service
delivery for the EDRG programme, risking the loss of experienced
staff to alternative employment, and potentially jeopardising the
Council's ability to deliver against GMCA grant conditions from 1
April 2026. The likelihood of material financial loss arises from
the risk that replacement recruitment costs and programme delivery
delays would significantly exceed the cost of maintaining
continuity.

It was recommended that the
Executive Member for Economy and Regeneration approves extending
the two posts outlined above to provide security for staff
affected, retain them in the Team and ensure the continued activity
and delivery of corporate priorities.

The following alternative
options were considered:
 
(a) Not to extend the posts:
This would result in the loss of two experienced officers,
disruption to EDRG programme delivery, and risk to the Council's
ability to meet GMCA grant conditions and maximise social value
outcomes.
 
(b) To extend on a temporary
basis only pending formal GMCA approval: While this would reduce
financial risk, it would not provide the employment stability
recommended by Human Resources and could result in the loss of
staff to more secure employment.
 
(c) To defer the decision until
after GMCA approval on 27 March 2026: This would leave insufficient
time to process contract extensions before 31 March and create
uncertainty for the staff affected.
 
On balance, the recommendation
as per the report provides the best outcome for service continuity
and staff retention.
 

None.
topline: The Executive Member for Economy and Regeneration has decided to continue funding two posts in Trafford's EDRG allocation 2026/2027 to ensure service continuity and staff retention.

decision_maker: Executive Member for Highways, Environmental, and Traded Services
purpose:
Opportunity has arisen from the Sale West & Altrincham
Network Improvement (SWANI) Funding Package, for improvement works
to 9 bus stop locations in the borough. This work will facilitate
construction of improved facilities for passengers boarding and
alighting at each of the stops with particular emphasis on an
improved experience for elderly, infirm or disabled people and
those using or pushing a wheelchair or pushchair. At the 9
locations, it is considered necessary to introduce a Bus Stop
Clearway ‘At Any Time’ in line with TfGM
guidance.
 
A
bus stop clearway is a designated area of the road, marked
with yellow lines and the words "BUS STOP", where vehicles are
prohibited from stopping, except for buses stopping to pick up or
drop off passengers. This restriction ensures buses can access
stops safely and efficiently, preventing obstruction from other
vehicles.  While there is no legal requirement to formally
advertise proposals for new bus stop clearways, frontages in the
vicinity of the pre-existing bus stops in question were consulted
on 28th March 2025. This consultation resulted in
receipt of 3 No. representations that are being considered as
objections to the proposals.
 
Having considered the contents of the comments received,
approval is sought to introduce the 9 No. bus stop clearways as
proposed, and as shown on drawing numbers SJ0442&0448-C-01,
SJ0423-C-01, SJ0425-C-01, SJ0451-C-01, SJ0453-C-01, SJ0361-C-01,
SJ1778-C-01, SJ4783-C-01.

The
Seymour Grove Phase 2 scheme is a Trafford Council (TC) promoted
scheme, to be funded through tranche 1 of the City Region
Sustainable Transport Settlement (CRSTS), and to provide a
strategic, high-quality cycle and walking route from Talbot Road
through Trafford to Chorlton.
 
The
Seymour Grove Scheme was originally proposed by TC in 2019 as part
of Mayoral Challenge Fund (MCF) application and was later split
into a Phase 1 and Phase 2. The Seymour Grove Phase 1 scheme, at
the junction at Seymour Grove and Talbot Road, was funded through
the MCF and is scheduled for completion in December
2025.
 
The
report summarises the outcomes of the consultation of the proposed
Seymour Grove Phase 2 Scheme and to recommend that the proposed
scheme and progress to detailed design stage and, subject to all
necessary CRSTS business case approvals, proceed to delivery as per
the programme of works.

1)   
That the content and findings of the consultation
report, be noted.
 
2)   
That it be noted that the scheme, incorporating
enhancements following input from the consultation, be progressed
to detailed design, and thereafter, subject to all necessary CRSTS
business case approvals, proceed to delivery.

 
3)   
That the programme as set out in Section 5 of the
report, be noted.

 
4)   
That the Corporate Director of Place, in
consultation with the Director of Finance and Systems, be delegated
authority to negotiate and finalise the grant funding agreements,
construction contracts and any other contracts or documents
required to implement the decision.
 
5)   
That the Director of Legal and Governance be
delegated authority to enter any contracts or other documents
required to implement the decision.

The
Seymour Grove Phase 2 Scheme will support and encourage sustainable
modes of transport for the surrounding communities, help to deliver
Trafford’s vision for inclusive and accessible neighbourhoods
and provide both the local and wider connections to other
high-quality strategic walking and cycling infrastructure along
GM’s Bee Active Network.
 
This
report forms part of an approval process of securing CRSTS funding
for the delivery of the scheme.
 
It
is recommended that the Seymour Grove Phase 2 Scheme progress to
detailed design stage and, subject to all necessary CRSTS business
case approvals, proceed to delivery as it supports Trafford’s
objectives of providing alternative sustainable active travel modes
of transport being used across the Borough that will benefit health
and wellbeing and air quality.

The
alternative options would include retaining the existing
arrangements, continuing to incur the costs of superficially
maintaining the outdated infrastructure and negative perceptions of
having unsafe pedestrian crossings and increasing levels of
severance along Seymour Grove.
 
A
second alternative would involve reducing the scope of the scheme
altogether; this would risk the scheme, not achieving its desired
objectives, not demonstrating sufficient economic benefits to
secure the CRSTS funding criteria and well as potentially not
future proofing this area as development occurs around it as
forecast.
 
Both
alternatives are missed opportunities to achieve the stated
outcomes as in the councils Walking, Wheeling, and Cycling strategy
of improving infrastructure and support towards reducing carbon
emissions. They would also impact on Trafford’s reputation
for securing future funding bids for other sustainable grant Active
Travel 9 opportunities that aim to encourage residents to be more
active and supporting people out of poverty by enabling affordable
transport.
topline: The Executive Member for Climate Change has decided to progress the Seymour Grove Phase 2 Scheme to detailed design stage and delivery, aiming to support sustainable transport and improve infrastructure in Trafford.

Dunham Massey Parish Council
wish to prepare a neighbourhood plan for The Dunham Massey Parish
area.
 
Dunham Massey Parish Council
requested for the whole Parish area to be formally designated a
“Neighbourhood Plan Area” by the Council by submitting
the request in writing on 3 November 2025.

To designate the entire Dunham
Massey Parish Council area to form a Neighbourhood Plan Area,
enabling the Parish Council to produce a Neighbourhood
Plan.

Dunham Massey Parish Council wish
to prepare a neighbourhood plan for The Dunham Massey Parish
area.
 
The Parish
Council have been in regular contact with the Strategic Planning
Team over a number of years to determine
when would be the most appropriate time to prepare the plan, having
regard to the Places for Everyone and Trafford Local
Plan.
 
Dunham Massey
Parish Council requested for the whole Parish area to be formally
designated a “Neighbourhood Plan Area” by the Council
by submitting the request in writing on 3 November
2025.
 
When a Parish
Council applies for the whole of its parish area to be designated
as a Neighbourhood Plan Area, the requirement for public
consultation in relation to the designation is removed under
Regulation 5A of the 2012 Regulations (introduced by the 2016
Amendment Regulations).
 
The Parish
Council has responsibility for writing the plan and Trafford
Council will be required to provide an advisory role in order to make sure the plan is consistent with
the Places for Everyone plan and emerging Trafford Local Plan.
Trafford Council will also need to provide high level advice on the
soundness and effectiveness of proposed policies.
 
The designation
of the Parish Council boundary as a Neighbourhood Plan area must be
published on the Council website.

There are no alternative
options. The Council has no power to refuse the designation of a
Neighbourhood Plan Area and must assist in the production of the
plan in line with regulations. As it is a Parish Council wishing to
designate the entire parish boundary, there is no need for
consultation on this.

None.
topline: The Corporate Director Place has decided to approve the Dunham Massey Parish Council's request to designate the entire parish area as a 'Neighbourhood Plan Area' for the preparation of a neighbourhood plan.

purpose:
This
report seeks approval to procure a new Open Framework contract for
the transport of pupils with SEND, children in social care and
vulnerable adults. Procurement is being led by STAR, the
council’s procurement partner, in collaboration with five
other Northwest local authorities.
 
The
new framework will be for eight years, starting in September 2026,
and will replace the current framework which ends in August 2026.
Based on current levels of demand, the annual cost of the transport
contract is estimated to be in the region of £7m for 2026/27
and £61m over the total contract.
 
Local authorities have a legal duty to provide free
home-to-school transport for eligible children of compulsory school
age (5–16) who have special educational needs and
disabilities (SEND), where their needs or distance from school make
them eligible. There are currently 900 children, young people and
adults accessing transport commissioned by Trafford Council, an
increase of 16% since academic year 2022/23.

purpose:
The One
Trafford Partnership has a prioritisation matrix for the assessment
of requests for 20mph speed limits across Trafford. Currently,
there are 87 requests on the matrix which have been assessed and
prioritised accordingly.
 
As a pre-requisite to a potential wider roll out
of 20mph speed limits in Trafford, a trial of 20mph speed limits,
or the alteration of existing 20mph zones has been considered and
agreed outside Abbotsford Preparatory School, Flixton Girls School
and Bowdon Preparatory School for Girls, in Flixton and Bowdon. It
is also proposed that ‘No Waiting at Any Time’ and
‘School Keep Clear’ restrictions are to be introduced
outside Flixton Girls School. The proposed measures are designed to
control parking away from the school entrance(s) and encourage more
parents and children to attend school on foot. The schemes also aim
to improve the overall traffic management around the school
entrance.
 
In addition, it is proposed to introduce a School
Safety Zone immediately outside Bowdon Preparatory School for
Girls. This is an advisory 20mph speed limit which operates at
school times. These are signed with flashing amber
lights.
 
To date, an informal consultation has been
undertaken with the local schools where these trials are set to
take place. Positive feedback was received from both the schools
and local Councillors.
 
In view of the above, it is considered
appropriate to promote the measures identified in the drawings
appended to this report.

Preparatory School for Girls, in Flixton and Bowdon. It is also
proposed that ‘No Waiting at Any Time’ and

outside Flixton Girls School. The proposed measures are designed to
control parking away from the school entrance(s) and encourage more

entrance.

report.

comments.

experienced.
topline: The Corporate Director Place has decided to introduce 20mph speed limits and parking restrictions outside schools in Trafford to improve traffic management and encourage walking to school.

content:
The report provides a summary
of the Examiner’s report and proposed modifications to the
Warburton Neighbourhood Development Plan (WNDP).
 
The report seeks approval of
the Examiner’s modifications to ensure that the WNDP meets
the Basic Conditions, which a draft neighbourhood plan must meet if
it is to proceed to referendum.
 
The report also seeks approval
for the WNDP to proceed to referendum and for the proposed area in
which the referendum is to take place.

1.         
That each of the
proposed modifications to the WNDP contained within the
Examiner’s report (Appendix 2), be approved.

 
2.         
That the WNDP should
proceed to referendum and that the Director of Growth and
Regulatory Services, in consultation with the Director of Legal and
Governance, be delegated authority to carry out any action required
to enable the WNDP to proceed to referendum.
 
3.         
That the referendum
boundary, as recommended by the Examiner (detailed in Appendix 1),
be approved.
 
4.         
That the Corporate
Director of Place be delegated authority
to approve other minor non-material changes (that do not affect the
Basic Conditions).
 
5.         
That it be noted that if the outcome of the referendum vote
supports the WNDP, it will go to Full Council to be formally
adopted as part of the Development Plan.

The Examiner concluded that the
WNDP has met the basic conditions and, subject to the policy
modifications set out in his report, should proceed to referendum.
Therefore, approval is sought to make the proposed modifications
(Appendix 2) to the WNDP as set out in the Examiner’s report,
to approve the referendum boundary and agree that the WNDP should
proceed to referendum under the direction of both the Director of
Growth and Regulatory Services and the Director of Legal and
Democratic Services.
 
To make a
decision to not take the WNDP forward to referendum in
accordance with the Examiner’s recommendations would be
contrary to the Neighbourhood Planning (General) Regulations 2012
(as amended by) The Neighbourhood Planning (General) (Amendment)
Regulations 2015.

The Examiner stated that the
WNDP has met the basic conditions, subject to modifications, and
therefore must proceed to referendum. Not to take the WNDP forward
would be contrary to the Examiner’s recommendations and
therefore the Regulations under the Town and Country Planning Act
1990 (as amended).
 
Some or all
of the Examiner’s recommendations could be
rejected/amended, which would result in a delay proceeding to
referendum. Because this would be contrary to the Examiner’s
recommendations, clear reason(s) for its change(s) to the
Modifications would need to be provided. It would also result in a
need for a further period of public consultation. Changing the
modifications could result in the WNDP not meeting the “basic
conditions’” test because the Examiner considered that
his modifications were necessary to ensure that the WNDP met this
test.

None.
topline: The Executive Member for Economy and Regeneration has decided to approve modifications to the Warburton Neighbourhood Development Plan for a referendum.

purpose:
The Trafford Housing
Allocations Policy has been updated due to changes in government
legislation and the limited availability of social and affordable
housing in the borough. The draft policy has been subject to public
consultation. The report summarises the consultation feedback and
outlines the final changes made to the policy.
content:
The Trafford Housing
Allocations Policy has been updated due to changes in government
legislation and the limited availability of social and affordable
housing in the borough. The draft policy has been subject to public
consultation. The report summarises the consultation feedback and
outlines the final changes made to the policy.

(1)      
That the Trafford Housing Allocations Policy 2025 be
approved for implementation and publication to comply with legal
framework outlined in Part 6 of the 1996 Housing Act.

 
(2)      
That the local connection exemptions for care
experienced young people, domestic abuse and armed forces veterans
be incorporated and implemented under the existing Trafford Housing
Allocations Policy.
 

To approve the Trafford Housing
Allocations Policy 2025, for the purposes of publication to ensure
the Council is compliant with Parts 6 and 7 of the Housing Act 1996
and has an up-to-date Policy in place to ensure a fair and
transparent process for the allocation of social and affordable
housing for the residents of Trafford.

Without adopting the
recommended legislative and guidance changes, Trafford could be in
breach of its public sector equality duty and subject to challenges
under housing legislation and would not be compliant with Parts 6
and 7 of the Housing Act 1996.  Trafford
therefore must make the legislative changes to ensure that the
policy remains compliant with current law and guidance issued by
the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local
Government.

None.
topline: The Executive Member for Housing and Advice has decided to update the Trafford Housing Allocations Policy to comply with legal requirements and ensure fair allocation of social and affordable housing.

content:
The report seeks approval for

Internationale de Football Association) for Trafford to be a Host
City for the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2035.


1.         
That approval, in principle, be given for the
Council to enter into an Agreement with FIFA (the Federation
Internationale de Football Association) for Trafford to be a Host
City for the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2035.
 

2.         
That the Corporate Director of Place, in
consultation with the Director of Finance and Systems and the
Director of Legal and Governance, be delegated authority to agree
the terms of the Agreement.
 

3.         
That the Director of Legal and Governance be
delegated authority to enter into any
documentation required to implement the recommendations set out
within the report.
 

To take advantage of the
opportunity to host a large sporting event in Trafford, aligning to
the Council’s Corporate Priorities and supporting delivery of
Trafford Moving and the borough’s Sport and Physical Activity
Strategy.
 
To benefit from the opportunity
to collaborate with a range of key stakeholders on the project,
including FIFA, the Football Association, UK government, Greater
Manchester Combined Authority, Manchester City Council, Manchester
United Football Club and Lancashire County Cricket Club, among
others.
 
To promote the positive
reputation of the Council, particularly through the promotion of
sport for women and girls.

from the bid at this stage. This would likely have a negative
impact on the Council’s reputation, particularly in light of the alignment between this opportunity

negative impact on the Council’s strong relationships with
various stakeholders; in particular, Manchester United Football
Club, Greater Manchester Combined Authority and the Football

negatively affected.

decision_maker: Executive Member for Healthy & Independent Lives
purpose:
The current contract for
substance misuse prevention and treatment is held by Salford City
Council who are procuring these services on behalf of themselves
and Trafford Borough Council (Trafford BC) and Bolton Council. The
current contract expires on 31st March 2026 following a one-year
extension to the original 5+2 year contract. A previous key
decision was made by Executive on 24th June 2024 to re-commission
these services with an updated specification. Following
negotiations with the intention to Direct Award under Health Care
Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, agreement
could not be reached on the financial envelope and existing
specification which meant that the terms and conditions of Direct
Award could not be met and therefore, a full open procurement
process was required. This has now concluded, pending final sign
off through Salford City Council’s Procurement Board.
Following the procurement process, the proposal is to award two new
5 year contracts each with an option to extend for 2 years –
one relating to adults and one relating to children and families.
The proposed future contracts will be held by Salford City Council
on behalf of Trafford Borough Council and Bury Council and the
relationship between Trafford BC and Salford City Council will be
supported by a Memorandum of Understanding, as has been the case
during the previous contracts.

report.

 
(2)

Wellbeing Board.

process enables the authority to build on this and progress the 11
recommendations in the JSNA with some stability due to recommission
of incumbent providers.
 
The current financial envelope
recognises the cumulative pressures of wage and wider inflation on
both NHS and community organisations but the envelope for the new
contracts has not been uplifted for inflation, reflecting the
significant pressures on the local authority and encouraging
innovation and efficiencies through the re[1]tender process.
